title: String Musical Instruments and Drawing
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Creative Arts; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Bring an improvised fiddle or a picture of the nyatiti, orutu, litungu and obokano. Community facts are for a teacher to confirm.

skills.key_step: The child names Kenyan string instruments (nyatiti, orutu, litungu, obokano), their community and whether they are plucked or bowed.

floor.question: Name a Kenyan string instrument.
floor.answer: any of: nyatiti, orutu, litungu, obokano

board.do: Show the orutu with its bow.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a string instrument?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: what do you do to make the sound? Pluck, bow, blow or hit? Sort five instruments by that one question.

listen_for: It is plucked with the fingers
misconceptions.repair: Look at pictures: the orutu has one string and a bow, the nyatiti has many strings and no bow.

misconceptions.ask: The nyatiti belongs to which people?
misconceptions.repair: Make a matching card: instrument, community, how it is played.

misconceptions.ask: Is the obokano a small fiddle or a large lyre?
misconceptions.repair: Show the size of the obokano next to a learner.

checks.question: Is the nzumari a string instrument?
checks.answer: No, it is a wind instrument

skills.key_step: The child says the strings vibrate to make sound, the body amplifies it, pegs tune it, and tighter or thinner strings give higher notes.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how wind instruments make sound (Grade 5).
floor.question: What vibrates in a flute?

steps: The hollow body makes it louder.
Turn the peg: tighter is higher.
contexts: tuning a fiddle before a performance

board.do: Write each part and its job.

misconceptions.ask: What does the hollow body of a string instrument do?
misconceptions.repair: Pluck a string held in the air and then over a tin: hear the tin make it louder.
Tighten a rubber band and pluck: hear it rise.

misconceptions.ask: Which string gives a higher sound?
misconceptions.repair: Tighten and loosen a rubber band and listen.

misconceptions.ask: Which string gives the lower note: a thick one or a thin one?
misconceptions.repair: Pluck a thick and a thin rubber band on a tin.

checks.question: What does the hollow body do?
What is the peg for?
checks.answer: tightening or loosening the string to tune it

skills.key_step: The child says stippling shades with small dots: dots close together make dark areas, spaced dots light areas.

floor.question: How does cross-hatching make an area darker?

steps: Space the dots out toward the light.

board.do: Draw a box and dot one end closely.

misconceptions.repair: Draw one patch with dots and one with lines and name them.

misconceptions.ask: How do you make a part of a stippled picture look dark?
misconceptions.repair: Make two squares, one with close dots and one with spaced dots, and ask which looks darker.

listen_for: Smudge the ink with a finger

misconceptions.ask: Should stippling dots be big blobs or small dots?
misconceptions.repair: Stipple a strip with fine dots and one with blobs; compare.

checks.question: How do you show a dark area in stippling?
